title: Prove narration plays by real playback
statement: Prove narration plays by observing real playback where media can play, since simulated media events test only fallback code.
detail: In a Grade 5 click-through the reading control looked active without proving that meaningful narration had started (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/docs/G5_STUDENT_EXPERIENCE_RELEASE_GATE.qmd`, line 20). The postmortem found that audio tests had simulated media events inside a network-blocked fixture, which proves recovery code, not playable narration (lines 61-62). The product contract now starts the read-to-me state only after real playback starts, not when a control is present or a request was attempted, and the release check needs a media-capable boundary that observes real playback, since a loopback failure can test fallback behaviour but cannot prove or disprove production media (lines 50-51 and 86).
